summary:
How really great that you’re going to have a baby! So are we, Tessa and I, as a matter of fact—yours will be born first, though, since ours isn’t due until July or August. We had planned to fly up to Canada, as I had told you, but financial problems got in the way; first, there was the World Science Fiction Convention here in Los Angeles in September and then, a month later, we had to fly up to 
San Francisco for my divorce action against my wife. We stayed in San Francisco four days. Tessa had never been there and enjoyed it a lot. But the trip destroyed us financially and wore me out; I had to cancel my speaking engagements throughout November, and then in December I got the flu. I’m just getting over it. 

It sounds wonderful that you’re at Salt Spring Island, now. Nearby here is a therapy center called the Tustin Rap Center, and one day when I was over there the man who founded it asked me where I’d been before Fullerton. When I said “Canada” he said, “I was up there—at Salt Spring.” It’s a small world. He told me how nice it is and I recall you all talking about it, especially what April said. Is she still with you? I think about her a lot; she was so bright and alert and nice—I liked her very much. I hope she’s doing fine; please let me know about her. In your previous letter you mentioned that Jim had had a couple of opera­ tions. Is he okay now? Let me know about that, too; I assume he is or you’d men­ tion otherwise.
